entities.summary: Pedro Sarmiento was a Spanish Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal, born into the nobility of the Kingdom of Granada and ordained to the priesthood in 1515. He played a key role in the Council of Trent, where he advocated for Catholic reform and the use of vernacular languages in liturgy. Sarmiento was appointed cardinal in 1539 and became a prominent figure in Spanish Catholicism, serving as a mediator between the Catholic Church and the Habsburg monarchs. He died on October 23, 1541, while on a pilgrimage to the shrine of St. Peter in Rome. Pedro Sarmiento's legacy as a champion of Catholic reform and his influence on the Council of Trent continue to be studied by historians today. The 'Sarmiento Reforms' of 1537, which he initiated, aimed to increase the use of vernacular languages in liturgy and promote greater priestly education, leaving a lasting impact on Spanish Catholicism.
